small_guidance:
- The kernel timed out during autotune likely because the inner loop nest is enormous (IC*KH*KW*POOL*POOL = 8*3*3*4*4 = 1152 static iterations) combined with large grid (N*OC*PH*PW/BLOCK_P = 128*64*96*96/BLOCK_P). Drop the large BLOCK_P configs (256, 512) and shrink the autotune set to 2-3 configs (e.g. BLOCK_P=64 num_warps=2/4, num_stages=2) to keep autotune time bounded.
- Restructure the loop so that the 4x4 pool window load is hoisted: for each (ic, kh, kw) load the 4x4 patch once and multiply by w_val, instead of re-reading via masked loads BLOCK_P times per pool element. Mask only on the spatial-tile boundary, not on every load.
- Fuse the avg-pool division into the bias add (`bias / (POOL*POOL)` is wrong — keep `pooled/(POOL*POOL) + bias`), and consider a 2D tile (BLOCK_PH x BLOCK_PW) to improve input-row reuse across pool windows.
large_guidance:
- Switch to an im2col-style GEMM where K = IC*KH*KW is the reduction axis and one program handles a tile of (OC, output-spatial) for a single batch. Then fuse a sigmoid+pool+sum epilogue: each program reduces its OC tile over its pooled spatial tile in registers and atomic-adds into out[n]. This avoids the deeply nested static loops that are blowing up compile/launch time.
- Alternatively, since OH*OW = 382*382 is moderate and OC=64, run a two-stage design: kernel 1 produces conv output with sigmoid(avg_pool(.)+bias) fused, writing per-(n, oc, ph, pw); kernel 2 does the sum reduction. This separates compute-heavy conv from the cheap reduction and lets each be tuned independently.
- For the conv kernel, use a direct-conv tiling with one program per (n, oc_tile, pooled_spatial_tile), loading a (POOL+KH-1)x(POOL+KW-1) input patch per ic into SRAM/registers and accumulating across ic. With IC=8 the K dimension is tiny so a full im2col GEMM may be overkill — a direct tiled conv with channels_last input layout and BLOCK_OC=32, BLOCK_PHW=32 is likely the right shape.
